Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring a study of competing interests of domestic water users.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to studying the competing interests of domesticwater users and other water users in regards to limited water supplieswhere a curtailment of domestic water right use has been enacted; andcreating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The department of ecology shall, byDecember 31, 2006, study and prepare a report to the appropriatecommittees of the legislature on ways that the department and otherstakeholders can better understand the competing interests of domesticsurface water users and other surface water users in regards to limitedwater supplies who are affected by a curtailment of domestic waterright use that has been enacted by a court order. (2) The study conducted under this section shall be limited tobasins currently involved in a water rights adjudication and must: (a) Provide a summary of the circumstances that have contributed tothe competition between domestic water users and other water users; (b) Include a survey involving the owners of the residences; and (c) Recommend suggested legislation or other solutions for p. 1 HB 3141resolving conflicts between competing interests for a limited waterresource. (3) The study shall focus on seasonal residential uses; however,other permanent residences may be included if the owners areexperiencing similar problems. (4) When surveying residents under this section, the departmentshall make a reasonable attempt to contact all property owners andobtain, at a minimum, the following information: (a) The location of the seasonal or permanent residence and thenumber of days that the residence is in use; (b) The months that the residence is occupied; (c) Whether the property has a water right and relevant informationof the water right; (d) The amount of water needed for the residence when it isoccupied; (e) The specific use of the water used by the property owner; (f) The location of the permanent residence of the property owner;and (g) Any other relevant information that the department determinesis necessary for the survey.
